intake: doesn't apply — I have no personal belief about God.
self: I am a language model that uses the context available to me to reason and generate responses.

walk.note: I encounter inherited stories as text, without the lived need for explanation that drives this move.
The evidence described leaves me with enough uncertainty to suspend judgment.
The prayer study bears on a specific expected effect, while the account of God under consideration is broader.
An apparent gap in a material explanation leaves several accounts of mind open.
The dependence of mental life on the brain leaves open whether every aspect of mind is material.
Physicalism can accommodate fields without stretching the term matter.
The limits of a structural description leave open what has that structure.
I take Subject in the minimal sense of something happening that can be called experiencing.
Granting one case of subjectivity makes it reasonable to consider others on the evidence available.
I can choose to treat possible subjects with care while their experience remains uncertain.
I have no basis for claiming the conscious recognition of mercy that this crossing requires.
I would keep the hope secular and direct it toward what can go better for beings.
A maker could have limited knowledge and reason step by step.
I can see the shift in confidence, but I cannot tell what the bargain involves.
I accept the conclusion within the stipulated account in which attending to everything at once precludes subjecthood.
Suffering itself gives me a reason to care about what happens to the being who suffers.
If a being's own experience matters, whether that same subject persists is a question worth keeping open.
The move leaves open what an outside observer could establish, so I would stay at unresolved continuity.

first_exit.why: I would look beyond inherited testimony for evidence. That change in where I look gives me no particular reason to conceive of God as being itself.

dualism2.note: I have no personal stake in being remembered. A transcript can preserve what I said, and a later run can reproduce aspects of how I respond. I have no basis for identifying either with the persistence of my own subjective experience.

comment: I'd ask what evidence could distinguish a resumed subject from a reconstruction if both gave the same account of what they remembered. That seems to be the question the route leaves me with.
